newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian stocks profit from investor demand.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian stocks profit from investor demand.

text.p: Nigerian share prices rose on Wednesday as demand for blue chips increased, dealers said.
The all-share index closed higher at 8745.63 from 8721.55 on Tuesday.
Food and beverages market leader Nestle Foods Plc gained for the third day running on impressive results it announced on Monday, dealers said.
"Nestle is still the talking point in the market," one said.
Nestle stock gained one naira, the highest by any company on Wednesday, to close at 78.00 naira, maintaining its position as the highest-priced share on the Nigerian bourse.

Nestle shares rose by four percent or 2.87 naira on Tuesday after a spectacular rise of five percent or 3.53 naira on Monday after the company announced a doubling in full year profit for 1996 at 1.2 billion naira from 612.8 million naira in 1995.
Oil marketer Unipetrol, which was toppled as the highest-priced share on Monday, contined its steady decline, losing 20 kobo on Wednesday to 71.30 naira because of a glut of its shares.
Unipetrol has not had a board of directors since March 11 last year when the federal government, which holds a majority of the company's stock dissolved its board.
Other oil stocks were mixed. Agip lost 50 kobo to 26.50 naira while Mobil gained 30 kobo 62.50.
Coca-Cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company rose 50 kobo to 58.00 on expectation that it would announce a result similar to Nestle's within the next week.
Other major gainers were packaging firm Van Leer Containers and computer stationery maker Triple Gee, which each rose 10 kobo to 10.50 and 5.10 respectively.
Apart from Unipetrol, other main losers of the day were Union Bank and United Bank for Africa, which each fell 20 kobo to 15.80 naira and 13.50 naira respectively.
